title: How Well Do You Know LitRPG?
dek: Ten questions on the genre's lingo and lore. Let's see your rank.

outcomes.name: Tutorial Zone
outcomes.tagline: Everyone starts somewhere, and you're about to have so much fun.
outcomes.description: You're new here, which is the best place to be: the whole genre is still ahead of you. Your results come with a starter list of beginner-friendly favorites.

questions.explain: Literature + RPG: stories where game mechanics are a real part of the world, and you see them on the page.
The name came out of Russia's game-fiction scene in 2013, when a major Russian publisher launched a LitRPG book line.

questions.prompt: When readers call a LitRPG "crunchy," they mean it has...

options.label: Lots of stats, numbers and mechanics on the page
A magic system based on snacks

questions.explain: Crunch is how much of the System you actually see: status screens, stat blocks, build math.

questions.prompt: In a "dungeon core" story, the main character is...

options.label: A blacksmith who sells gear to adventurers

questions.explain: In dungeon core stories you're the dungeon: building floors, designing traps and raising monsters.

questions.prompt: What mainly separates progression fantasy from LitRPG?

options.label: Progression fantasy doesn't need visible stats or a game System
Progression fantasy is always set on Earth

questions.explain: Both are about getting stronger. LitRPG shows the game mechanics; progression fantasy can grow the hero's power without any status screens.

questions.prompt: "Isekai" is a Japanese term for stories where the hero...

options.label: Is transported or reborn into another world

questions.explain: Isekai roughly means "another world": the hero is transported, summoned or reborn somewhere new.

questions.prompt: In cultivation stories, characters mainly grow stronger by...

options.label: Refining qi or spiritual energy through realms

questions.explain: Cultivation comes from Chinese xianxia and wuxia fiction: cultivators refine energy to break through one realm after another.

questions.prompt: What happens in a "System Apocalypse" story?

options.label: A game-like System arrives on Earth and everything changes
The world ends in chapter one and nothing else happens

questions.explain: The System shows up, monsters spawn, and everyone on Earth has to level up or die trying.

questions.prompt: A "regression" story is one where the main character...

options.label: Goes back to an earlier point in their life, keeping their memories
Moves back in with their parents
Relives the same day over and over

questions.explain: Regressors get one do-over with future knowledge. Reliving the same stretch again and again is a time loop.

questions.prompt: Which site is best known as the home of free LitRPG and progression fantasy web serials?
questions.explain: A huge share of the genre's hits started as free serials on Royal Road before becoming books and audiobooks.
